introduction: My research interests connect geospatial AI, 3D scene understanding, and autonomous spatial data processing. At HawarIT Limited, I have developed systems across aerial imagery, LiDAR, GIS validation, and urban reconstruction. I aim to build on this engineering experience through research into reliable automation and digital twins.

modules.title: Orthophoto pipeline automation
modules.summary: Camera alignment, image quality assessment, and spatial validation for aerial mapping.

blocks.heading: Engineering experience
blocks.body: I developed feature-matching and tie-point workflows for aerial camera alignment, with reported 2-pixel alignment accuracy and a 90% reduction in manual aerial triangulation effort. My image quality assessment work detected cloud, shadow, and blur with reported 97% accuracy. Seamline optimization using PostgreSQL/PostGIS and AHN LiDAR reduced manual editing by 65%.

blocks.heading: Research direction
blocks.body: I would investigate how geometric constraints and image quality models can be combined into a reliable orthophoto production pipeline. Further questions include automated DEM refinement and true-orthophoto validation around building edges, bridges, and elevated structures.

modules.title: 3D spatial modeling and digital twins
modules.summary: Structured urban geometry and photorealistic reconstruction from aerial observations.

blocks.heading: Engineering experience
blocks.body: I built automated CityGML reconstruction and multi-view aerial texture projection workflows. View selection and occlusion handling maintained reported texture displacement below 3 pixels.

blocks.heading: Research direction
blocks.body: I am interested in connecting CityGML representations with 3D Gaussian Splatting for photorealistic urban digital twins. Proposed extensions include video-based reconstruction using structure from motion and multi-view stereo, with attention to consistency at city scale.

modules.title: Remote sensing and change detection
modules.summary: Understanding physical change across multi-temporal aerial and satellite imagery.

blocks.heading: Engineering experience
blocks.body: I developed building change detection for construction, demolition, and extensions from multi-year orthophotos. Integrated into a GIS validation platform, the system achieved reported 88% accuracy and reduced manual inspection by 65%. My Sentinel multispectral analytics work covered crop classification, water quality, and algae bloom detection; the framework placed second in an international innovation tender.

blocks.heading: Research direction
blocks.body: I would investigate how models distinguish physical changes from seasonal variation, lighting, shadows, and sensor differences. A further direction is adapting these methods to post-disaster infrastructure assessment.

modules.title: Point cloud intelligence and spatial understanding
modules.summary: Semantic and geometric understanding of LiDAR and street-view observations.

blocks.heading: Engineering experience
blocks.body: I developed semantic segmentation and pipe/geometry extraction across aerial, mobile, and indoor LiDAR, with reported 95% extraction accuracy and a 60% reduction in manual processing time. My street-view GeoAI pipeline used YOLOv5 and tracking for 130 traffic sign and 33 street furniture classes, with reported detection accuracy above 95% and localization precision of 92%.

blocks.heading: Research direction
blocks.body: I am interested in turning unstructured point clouds and imagery into consistent, semantically annotated CAD/BIM objects for digital twins. Research questions include robust geometric extraction and reliable integration of observations from different acquisition platforms.

modules.title: Biomedical signal processing and explainable AI
modules.summary: The academic foundation of my work in signal analysis and interpretable machine learning.

blocks.heading: Undergraduate thesis
blocks.body:
*Quantifying Locomotive Features in EEG of Impaired Consciousness (Coma) with Distinctive Cerebral Rhythms.* I analyzed EEG time series and distinctive cerebral rhythms during my B.Sc. at IUT.

[IUT repository](https://repository.iutoic-dhaka.edu/items/e79be58c-22b4-4817-9329-05b0915d8160) · [Thesis PDF](/files/Mohammad_Mahmudul_Hasan_BSc_Thesis.pdf)

blocks.heading: Peer-reviewed work
blocks.body:
I co-authored “Demystifying Deep Learning Models for Retinal OCT Disease Classification using Explainable AI” (IEEE CSDE, 2021), studying retinal OCT classification and LIME-based interpretation.

[Publication details](/publication/retinal-oct-explainable-ai/) · [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1109/CSDE53843.2021.9718400)

thesis.title: Quantifying Locomotive Features in EEG of Impaired Consciousness (Coma) with Distinctive Cerebral Rhythms
thesis.summary: My undergraduate research examined EEG time-series signals and distinctive cerebral rhythms to identify features related to impaired consciousness. This work formed the signal-processing foundation of my later interests in machine learning and intelligent systems.
